articles.title: Skills over MCP: 21 checks, run on Hugging Face's 25 skills
articles.excerpt: Originally published on mcpscore.dev. Tools give an agent operations. A skill tells it how to combine them: a SKILL.md with instructions, plus the references and scripts it points to. Since the Skills…
articles.body: Originally published on mcpscore.dev . Tools give an agent operations. A skill tells it how to combine them: a SKILL.md with instructions, plus the references and scripts it points to. Since the Skills extension (SEP-2640) became final in September, an MCP server can serve skills next to its tools. mcpscore 1.27.0 checks them with 21 rules, and we ran them on the 25 skills Hugging Face serves. What a skill looks like on the wire A server that serves skills declares io.modelcontextprotocol/skills in its capabilities. Each file of a skill is an MCP resource, under a skill:// URI. skills/list returns one entry per skill: the URI of its SKILL.md , the frontmatter of that file as JSON, and the complete list of the skill’s files with a SHA-256 digest and a size for each.
articles.author: Alex Akimov

articles.title: SARIF explained: why linters speak it, and how mcpscore 1.14.0 writes it
articles.excerpt: Originally published on mcpscore.dev. A finding that lives in a CI log gets read once, by whoever opened the log. A finding in your repository’s Security tab gets an owner, a history, and a close date…
articles.body: Originally published on mcpscore.dev . A finding that lives in a CI log gets read once, by whoever opened the log. A finding in your repository’s Security tab gets an owner, a history, and a close date. SARIF is the format that moves findings from the first place to the second, and mcpscore 1.14.0 writes it. This post explains what SARIF is, why a linter should speak it, and exactly what mcpscore puts in the file. What SARIF is SARIF, the Static Analysis Results Format, is an OASIS standard : a JSON document that describes what an analysis tool found. Version 2.1.0 is the one everything reads. The shape is small. A file holds one or more runs . A run names the tool that produced it and the rules it applied, then lists results .

articles.title: Day 29: Managing Technical Debt, Drift and Model Governance in Enterprise IT
articles.excerpt: Shipping a model is not the finish line. Ordinary software stays exactly as correct as it was on release day until someone changes the code. An AI system can get worse without anyone touching it, beca…
articles.body: Shipping a model is not the finish line. Ordinary software stays exactly as correct as it was on release day until someone changes the code. An AI system can get worse without anyone touching it , because the world feeding it keeps moving. That slow decay is called drift , and managing it is the heart of long-term AI maintenance. In plain terms: A map is accurate the day it is printed. A year later new roads exist, and the map still looks confident while sending you down a closed street. Diagram: Data drift happens when the distribution of production inputs moves away from the training data, for example when a firmware update changes the units a device reports. The model was never trained on the new range, so its accuracy degrades quietly. See the animated version . 1.

articles.title: Authentication in SPAs: 8 Ways to Handle Tokens and Sessions
articles.excerpt: Authentication is one of those things that looks simple until you start thinking about security, token storage, session expiration, and multiple browser tabs. You can store a JWT in localStorage, keep…
articles.body: Authentication is one of those things that looks simple until you start thinking about security, token storage, session expiration, and multiple browser tabs. You can store a JWT in localStorage , keep an access token in memory, use HttpOnly cookies, or introduce a Backend for Frontend (BFF). Each approach comes with different trade-offs. The important question isn't just how to log users in. It's how to keep them authenticated without exposing their credentials unnecessarily. 1. Memory + Silent Refresh Keep the access token in JavaScript memory and the refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie. When the access token expires, the client calls a refresh endpoint. The browser automatically sends the cookie, and the backend issues a new access token.

articles.body: Resposta curta Dados sensíveis em saúde são categorizados como tais pela LGPD (art. 5º, XII) e exigem tratamento com base legal específica — geralmente consentimento explícito ou hipóteses de exceção previstas no art. 11 — além de medidas técnicas e organizacionais reforçadas. O Conselho Federal de Medicina (CFM) exige, ainda, conformidade com a Resolução CFM nº 2.288/2021, que estabelece critérios éticos e de segurança para o uso de dados pessoais em contextos clínicos e de pesquisa. TL;DR Dados sensíveis em saúde incluem informações sobre condição física ou mental, origem racial/étnica, vida sexual, convicções religiosas e dados genéticos (LGPD, art. 5º, XII). articles.title: 15 deterministic tools your AI agent should call instead of guessing
articles.excerpt: Ask an LLM whether EKU9003173C9 is a valid Mexican RFC, what the German VAT rate was on a given date, or which HTS code applies to a stainless steel sink, and you get a confident answer. Sometimes it…
articles.body: Ask an LLM whether EKU9003173C9 is a valid Mexican RFC, what the German VAT rate was on a given date, or which HTS code applies to a stainless steel sink, and you get a confident answer. Sometimes it is right. For an invoicing, KYC or customs agent, "sometimes" is not good enough: a check digit is either correct or not, a tariff code is either in the official schedule or not, and a payroll withholding comes from a published table, not from a model's memory. This post is about the class of work an agent should delegate to deterministic tools and how we packaged 15 of them as one MCP server on Apify . Everything runs against official or open sources, has no LLM inside, stores nothing, and costs half a cent per call. What belongs in a tool, not in a prompt Three tests.

articles.title: What I Built...
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the MLH x DEV Writing Challenge. During the hackathon, I worked on a voice agent — a project that explored making interactions with technology feel more natural through voice.…
articles.body: This is a submission for the MLH x DEV Writing Challenge . What I Built During the hackathon, I worked on a voice agent — a project that explored making interactions with technology feel more natural through voice. The idea was to move beyond the usual text-based interactions and explore a more conversational way for people to communicate with software. Building it meant figuring things out as I went, experimenting with the available tools, and trying to turn an idea into something that actually worked. The experience was hectic, with a lot happening in a short amount of time. Looking back, what stands out isn't every technical detail but the process itself: making decisions under pressure, troubleshooting unexpected issues, and learning by building.

articles.title: NASA-funded Study Details One of Oldest Mars Meteorites Ever Found
articles.excerpt: When a rose-colored meteorite was found in the Sahara Desert in 2022, no one knew how old it was or where it came from. Not until NASA-funded scientists age-dated its minerals did they realize the nea…
articles.body: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Called Teghaza 001, this rose-colored rock is one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth. Credit: © Darryl Pitt / Maine Mineral & Gem Museum When a rose-colored meteorite was found in the Sahara Desert in 2022, no one knew how old it was or where it came from. Not until NASA-funded scientists age-dated its minerals did they realize the nearly 2-pound (800-gram) rock was a piece of Mars that formed more than 4.1 billion years ago, making it one of the oldest Martian meteorites ever found. Named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered, the meteorite is one of roughly 435 from the Red Planet.

articles.excerpt: Two zombie exoplanets that rose from the grave to shuffle through the gory remains of their fellow planets may just agree with these immortal words from horror maestro Stephen King.
articles.body: "Sometimes dead is better." Who can forget the immortal words of Jud Crandall, delivered by the incomparable Fred Gwynne in the 1989 film adaptation of Stephen King's Pet Sematary? Turns out Crandall could have been talking about somewhere just as otherworldly as the cursed Chumash burial ground at the heart of one of King's most terrifying works of fiction. That's because astronomers have discovered two husks of two zombie planets shuffling through the gory remains of what was once their planetary neighbors around a long-deceased star, or white dwarf. The shattered planets were revealed by a clear gap in the debris around the white dwarf J1328−1450, located around 1,600 light-years away from Earth.

articles.title: Big cats, unexplained lights and a floodlit eclipse — 7 skywatching 'horror stories' to keep you entertained this Halloween
articles.excerpt: Stargazing doesn't always go to plan, and we have the stories to prove it.
articles.body: Halloween is almost upon us! To celebrate we've pulled together a series of short "skywatching horror stories" perfect for getting you in the mood for the spooky season. Granted, stargazing may not be the most hazardous of past times. But you'd be surprised how often things can go wrong. The best laid plans can be shattered by the unforeseen, unexpected phenomena can leave you scared witless, or mother nature itself can step in to remind us how little control we have over the environment around us. Many of the stories serve as a cautionary tale, while others are simply..unfortunate. Be sure to share your stories of skywatching "horror stories" in the comments below for a chance to feature in next year's Halloween coverage!
